translationRepairs: When Gaozu was besieged at Taiyuan, he personally braved arrows and stones, repeatedly offering sound advice at Gaozu's side, and Gaozu came to esteem him even more highly.
When Gaozu was besieged at Taiyuan, the future emperor personally braved arrows and stones and repeatedly offered sound counsel at Gaozu's side; Gaozu came to value him all the more.

The prior English makes Gaozu the natural antecedent of 'he,' but the chapter's subject, marked 帝, is the one who braved the missiles and offered counsel. The final 高祖愈重焉 then states Gaozu's growing regard for him.

On bingzi, Minister of Education and concurrent Palace Attendant Feng Dao was appointed commissioner for the late emperor's mausoleum, with Vice Director of the Chancellery Dou Zhengu as deputy; Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Cui Rong was made ritual commissioner; Vice Minister of Revenue Lü Qi was made procession commissioner; and Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Yijian was made ceremonial guard commissioner.

On bingzi, Minister of Education and concurrent Palace Attendant Feng Dao was appointed commissioner for the late emperor's mausoleum, with Vice Director of the Chancellery Dou Zhengu as deputy; Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Cui Zhuo was made ritual commissioner; Vice Minister of Revenue Lü Qi was made procession commissioner; and Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Yijian was made ceremonial guard commissioner.
The source names 崔棁, read Cui Zhuo. 'Cui Rong' is an unsupported misreading of the same graph and should not be retained as an alternate name.

On gengshen, Cui Rong, ritual commissioner for the mausoleum and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was posthumously made Mentor of the Heir Apparent with detached service in the Western Capital, having died of illness.

On gengshen, Cui Zhuo, ritual commissioner for the mausoleum and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was appointed Mentor to the Heir Apparent with detached service in the Western Capital because he was ill.
The name is Cui Zhuo. In addition, 病故也 gives illness as the reason for the detached Western Capital appointment; it does not say that a posthumous appointment followed his death.
